text:
sara: Heads up — I ran into a tenant fairness regression on staging. A small org is getting hammered by a bursty partner, their latencies spike and our smoothing doesn't kick fast enough.
omar: Can you paste the traces / logs? Is this a routing hot-spot or quota enforcement lag?
sara: Traces look like normal routing, but the per-key burst window is static (60s). When partner sends repeated short requests (10–20 tokens each, 100/s for ~20s), the tenant hits a downstream queue and stays degraded for ~3m.
marta: Ugh. Static windows were always a blunt instrument. We need adaptive windows that tighten on observed burstiness.
liam: Proposal: per-org EWMA of short-term token rate + percentile burst score to scale the smoothing window. If burst_score > threshold, shrink window from 60s -> 10s for that org, and back off slowly.
sara: Exactly. Also add a hard cap so we don't punish noise incorrectly. I sketched a config prototype:

```
# adaptive smoothing config (pseudo)
adaptive_window:
  base_seconds: 60
  min_seconds: 8
  max_seconds: 300
  ewma_alpha: 0.2    # responsiveness to new bursts
  p90_multiplier: 0.5
  backoff_half_life: 45s
```

omar: How do we compute the burst_score? Simple idea: ratio = current_rate / ewma_rate; burst_score = percentile_over_1m(ratio, 95).
kena: We should surface this on the console per-org so customers see why they got smoothed. UI needs: current window, burst_score, recent spikes.
liam: Telemetry: emit these metrics per-tenant (labels org_id): `burst_ratio_p90`, `adaptive_window_s`, `ewma_rate_tps`, `queue_fill`.

marta: From SRE side, add alert if a single tenant causes >30% queue_fill for >2m. That helps noisy-neighbor detection across nodes.
sara: Also want to avoid oscillations with canary rollout. Start by enabling adaptive window in staging for a subset (by tenant tag) and keep a fallback to static policy.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout step queued: enable `adaptive_window` flag for tag `burst-test` on staging cluster in 10m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

omar: For datastore and metrics cost, use summary metrics aggregated client-side: store counters + compute percentile on time-series backend (Prometheus histogram approach). Example query: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(burst_ratio_bucket[1m])) by (le, org_id))`.
kena: UX question: should the console let users opt-out of adaptive smoothing (for paid contracts)? We need policy guardrails — opt-out only for dedicated capacity or explicit SLA.
liam: Agreed. Default adaptive == on for hosted; opt-out allowed with approval and audit log. Add `adaptive_opt_out` flag to org metadata.

marta: Edge case: multi-key customers where one key is noisy but org-level smoothing penalizes others. We should support per-key overrides: apply window at the granularity that correlates best with the noisy signal (key vs org).
sara: Good catch. Implementation: compute burst signals at key level and roll up to org. If a single key is the source, mark that key for tighter window rather than org-wide.

omar: Next steps I volunteer for: implement metric emissions + config knobs in rate-limiter; add unit tests for backoff/fast-recovery. sara/kena can spec console surface, marta will add alerting rules.
sara: Awesome. Can we sync tomorrow 10am to walk the config and the Prom queries? I'll post the staging traces before then.
kena: 10am works. I'll draft console mockups.

liam: One more thought — add a cheap simulation job that replays recent traffic for a tenant to estimate impact of different windows before applying in prod.
sara: Love it. That will help avoid regression surprises.

marta: Quick note — ensure audit logging emits `reason=adaptive_smoothing` with metric snapshot for every throttle event. We need that for postmortem and customer questions.
sara: Agreed.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: adaptive_window feature flag scheduled for `burst-test` tag on staging at 2027-01-15T15:10:00Z.

sara: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the doc for the rollout checklist. I'll upload the traces and configs to the staging ticket.
liam: :thumbsup:
